statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. The weekend venue closure leaves no live Nasdaq-100 price path, so Tail remains far below the block threshold, while Stress stays elevated on hawkish rate repricing and an escalating US-Iran tanker exchange around the Strait of Hormuz.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Conditional risk is concentrated in the narrow 22:00-02:00 UTC futures-reopen window rather than across the whole session; existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: OPEC+ holds October output as US-Iran tanker exchange runs into a thin 22:00 UTC futures reopen before US Labor Day
body: CME equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00 UTC, so no live Nasdaq-100 price path is observable at this assessment. The last verified tape remains Friday September 4: ^NDX closed 29,544.15 (+0.21%) inside a 29,440.15-29,655.22 range, a mid-range finish with no session-extreme hold, and VIX ended at 14.53 after a 13.80-14.58 day range. Two verified developments have printed since the previous hourly assessment. First, key OPEC+ members including Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman held October output policy unchanged at an online meeting on Sunday, ending six consecutive monthly increases and scheduling the next meeting for October 4; the decision removes an incremental supply-relief path without adding a new price mechanism while the venue is shut. Second, Iran's chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said on Sunday that the era of proportionate responses is over and that future responses would be faster, heavier and more painful, which sharpens reopen gap risk without being observable in price. The underlying escalation is unchanged: US Central Command reported three Iranian crude tankers permanently disabled or destroyed on September 5 after Iranian ballistic missiles were fired toward a US carrier and destroyer, and the IRGC navy claimed strikes on three tankers plus three US-linked vessels. Brent settled Friday at 96.28 dollars, its highest since July 24 and more than 8 percent higher on the week, with reported Hormuz transits near 13 vessels per day. The rates backdrop is unchanged: the August employment report printed 162,000 payrolls against roughly 56,000 consensus with unemployment steady at 4.1 percent, lifting implied odds of a 25bp hike at the September 15-16 FOMC to roughly 58 percent, and H.15 still shows the September 3 readings of 2Y 4.34 percent and 10Y 4.77 percent. The pre-FOMC communications blackout began September 5 and runs through September 17. Shared delayed cross-asset context was collected at 11:23 UTC and is past its freshness threshold at this assessment, so it is used only as weak latest-session confirmation; on that basis Friday megacaps were 3 up and 5 down with a -1.22 percent mean while all seven tracked semiconductors were higher, a directionally mixed picture that reduces conviction rather than amplifying Tail. Because no live price path exists, no directional efficiency, shallow-pullback sequence or failed retracement can be observed, so Tail is held in the low band at 5 and the conditional risk is placed in the 22:00 UTC reopen hour, where unresolved escalation would be absorbed by the thinnest order book of the week. Stress stays elevated at 57 on the unresolved rates and energy backdrop. US cash equity markets are closed on Monday September 7 for Labor Day; the next verified checkpoints are the NFIB survey on September 8, August PPI on September 10 and August CPI on September 11.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available. Tail held flat at 4-5 with EA_ON and green throughout, while Stress rose from 41 during Saturday's European afternoon to 57 around the Saturday evening tanker exchange, then oscillated between 52 and 57 across the remaining weekend closure and finished the window at 56. Confidence stayed in an 84-86 band and dominant mode was normal for every hour.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover nine further closed hours, the 22:00 UTC futures reopen, and an Asian and European session on a US Labor Day holiday. Conditional Tail stays inside the low band except for the single reopen hour, which reaches 21 and maps to WATCH where an unresolved Hormuz tanker exchange and fresh Iranian escalation rhetoric meet the thinnest depth of the week, before decaying toward 8-9 as two-way discovery is assumed to resume. Stress peaks near 68 at the reopen on the combined rates and energy backdrop before unwinding toward 55. No US macro release falls inside the window, US cash equities are closed on September 7 for Labor Day and the Fed is in its pre-FOMC blackout; the next scheduled checkpoints are the NFIB survey on September 8, August PPI on September 10 and August CPI on September 11, ahead of the September 15-16 FOMC.
